Reading warm and cool colors in this NASA frame…

The live sound is an artistic mapping of colors sampled from each frame, not a thermometer reading. Red means warmer than the 1951–1980 average; blue means cooler. The frame shows a five-year running average of global surface temperature anomaly, not Dhaka’s air temperature.

CALM CONDITIONS

Middle notes, an even beat, and gentle chords.

Higher heat → higher melody. More rain → quicker drum. Less greenery → thinner, uneasy chords. Sound is always paired with words and color.

DATA DESK / TRANSPARENCY

What’s real, what’s a game?

Real visual frames

The 1884 and 2022 global temperature anomaly frames come from NASA SVS visualization 5060, featured in the Earth Information Center temperature view. NASA/GISS data; baseline 1951–1980; five-year running averages. Visual credit: NASA Scientific Visualization Studio.

Real Dhaka heat maps

Each observed city year shows a NASA GIBS rendering of Terra MODIS eight-day daytime land surface temperature (MOD11A2) around Dhaka. The requested viewing dates are April 15 in 2000, 2010, 2020, and 2024. The 2024 observation remains visible in the imagined future rounds as a reference. Land surface temperature differs from air temperature; cloud cover and sensor limits can leave gaps. These snapshots alone do not establish a climate trend.

Live sound mapping

The browser scans each global NASA frame from left to right. Warm and cool colors have separate voices; vertical position sets pitch, and pixel brightness sets loudness. The stereo position follows the scan. This original sound design adapts the approach described in NASA's cosmic sonification examples. The tones are an artistic translation of image colors, not measured degrees Celsius.

Dhaka game model

The named districts, warmer signals, coins, intervention effects, scores, and 2035/2050 paths are illustrative teaching mechanics. They are not traced from the MODIS map and do not represent measured neighborhood conditions, proven intervention effects, or NASA forecasts. NASA MODIS/VIIRS fire hotspots were not used for this urban heat game because they locate active fires and other intense thermal anomalies.
